title: A Relationship Between Nonphysical Quasi-probabilities and Nonlocality Objectivity

predicted_errors.error_location: Eq. (8) (computation of β^Tβ for semi-trivial perp states)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: For p = i⊗I the matrix β has only one nonzero row v = (β_ix, β_iy, β_iz), so β^Tβ = v^T v is the rank-1 outer product, with eigenvalues (|v|², 0, 0) — it is NOT the diagonal matrix diag(β_ix², β_iy², β_iz²) claimed in (8). (Note also that the two displayed objects in (8) are written as 3×1 columns, while β^Tβ must be 3×3.) With the correct computation, M = Σ_j β_ij² in the right-identity case, exactly the same value as in the left-identity case, so the claimed asymmetry — the entire basis for swap-intolerant nonlocality — does not exist.

Qubit swapping maps β → β^T, hence β^Tβ → ββ^T. For square matrices A, B the products AB and BA have the same characteristic polynomial, so β^Tβ and ββ^T have identical eigenvalues and the Horodecki quantity M = u + ū is invariant under qubit relabelling for ANY 2-qubit coefficient matrix (physical or not). Therefore 'swap-intolerant nonlocal' states cannot exist, and the central claim of the abstract ('states that are nonlocal under one component labelling but local when the labelling is interchanged') and Theorem 1.4 are false as stated.

The four quantities listed in (7) sum to (1+τ_p)+(1+τ_p)+(1−τ_p)+(1−τ_p) = 4, contradicting Tr(ρ)=1 required in Eq. (2). The eigenvalues of ρ = ¼(I + Σ c_ij σ_i⊗σ_j) carry an overall factor 1/4 (e.g. for ρ = ¼(I + c ZZ) the eigenvalues are (1±c)/4, not 1±c). Consequently the construction in the proof of Theorem 1.4 yields a smallest eigenvalue λ₀/4, not λ₀.

predicted_errors.error_location: Paragraph after Proposition 2.1 ('under translations and rotations of the parameter space S ... is unchanged')
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Only rotations (and reflections) of S preserve the eigenvalues. A translation E → E+t, C → C+t leaves |E−C| fixed but changes |(−E)−C| → |E+C+2t|, so the second family of eigenvalues in (7) is not invariant. Positive semidefiniteness is therefore not preserved under translations, contrary to the stated claim (the later argument only needs rotations, so the statement is unnecessarily and incorrectly general).

Eq. (7) gives eigenvalues 1+τ_p ± |E+C| and 1−τ_p ± |E−C| (with C the point of coordinates τ_i), i.e. positivity requires |E+C| ≤ r₊ and |E−C| ≤ r₋. Proposition 2.1 states the opposite pairing: 'E and its reflected point −E are contained ... in the spheres (C,r₊), (C,r₋) respectively'. The two statements are inconsistent as written (they differ by the sign convention for C).

predicted_errors.error_location: Conclusion ('the boundary for nonlocality in general in this case (including swap-intolerant nonlocality) is the same as the boundary for positive semidefiniteness ... |E| = 1')
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Within the paper's own framework, Eq. (8) gives for the right-identity case M = β₁²+β₂² (the two largest eigenvalues of a diagonal matrix), so the nonlocality boundary in that labelling is β₁²+β₂² = 1, not |E| = β₁²+β₂²+β₃² = 1. The concluding claim that the nonlocality boundary coincides with the positive-semidefiniteness boundary |E| = 1 'in general in this case (including swap-intolerant nonlocality)' therefore contradicts Eq. (8) and the SIN conditions (9) used earlier.

predicted_errors.error_location: Introduction: 'first described by Bell in 1964 [1], with an experimentally testable inequality discovered in 1966 [2]'
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The experimentally testable (CHSH) inequality was proposed by Clauser, Horne, Shimony and Holt in 1969, not 1966. Bell's 1966 paper is a review of hidden-variable theories and does not contain an experimentally testable inequality.

The Horodecki criterion is a necessary and sufficient condition for violation of the CHSH inequality, not for nonlocality per se (states with M ≤ 1 can still be nonlocal via other Bell inequalities, sequential measurements, etc.). Stating 'describes a nonlocal state iff M > 1' misrepresents the cited result and the strength of the paper's conclusions about locality under qubit swapping.

predicted_errors.error_location: Introduction: 'in 1995 the Horodecki brothers gave an equivalent mathematical statement [3]'
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The authors of the 1995 criterion (R., P. and M. Horodecki) are a father and his two sons, not three brothers; the attribution as 'the Horodecki brothers' is factually incorrect.

References [1]–[7] are cited throughout the text (Bell, CHSH, Horodecki, the hyperplane-states paper [4], doily references [5,6,7]) but only entry [8] appears in the reference list, so none of the key attributions can be verified.
